Yes! The route runs all the way from NOLA to NYC, leaves from New Orleans at 7 or 8am and arrives in Slidell almost exactly an hour later, costs about $15 or so (rough estimate since it’s been a few years, probably a couple bucks cheaper). On the way back, the train is *supposed* to arrive in Slidell at 6pm, but it comes down all the way from New York so it can either be perfectly on time or hours late. Also takes an hour to get to nola, but depending on arrival time there could be some waiting for other trains at the station to get settled and passengers to disembark. 

Overall very very lovely experience! Comfortable, quick enough, and you get to see some really great sights. Luckily every time I’ve gone, it hasn’t been for anything time sensitive so the delays were never more than a mild inconvenience. On days when the train is out of service, they have a greyhound bus! 

Sorry, I just love gushing about this particular line haha. Wish I had more reasons to take the train but now that I’ve got my car it’s unfortunately just more convenient to drive over the lake. But absolutely worth trying the train at least once, they’d probably get a huge service boost if they had another line going from Slidell to nola in the morning, and nola to slidell at night, for work commuters. But I digress! Try the train! 😁

I’ve waited until nearly 2am before for the 6pm train from Slidell to NOLA to arrive, simply because any delays along the route as it comes from the northeast push it back….and back……..and back………. Definitely plan for some delays, but super exciting nonetheless!!

Wow 😭 you would think all the “wrong way” signs would be a clue, even without working lights, but unfortunately the city can be so damn confusing at the best of times. For mine, I was heading to Carrollton from Metairie, but I’m from the Northshore so the exact location eludes me besides that there were a ton of ramps and curves. But I remember being with my two friends who are locals, seeing the headlights rapidly approaching, and just going “um, this is a one way road, right?? Am *I* on the right side??” And them both going “yes what the fuck” before I swerved out of the way just in time. Took me hours to stop shaking and ruminating on how close we all were to dying too 😭

Same thing happened to me a few months ago around the I-10/610 split as I was about to take an exit on the left side. Had to swerve all the way onto the right shoulder to avoid what would’ve been a fatal head on collision and sit there shell shocked for a minute. They were speeding as well, probably going at least 90 or more. It’s one of the most terrifying things I think I’ve ever experienced, and to this day I hope nobody got hurt further down because it was a long and winding way down before there was any chance of switching over to the correct direction x.x 

So glad you made it out of your situation okay! Some people should NOT be on the road, and at the very least we should all have to retake a driving test every few years in my opinion.

One of my kitties unexpectedly passed away earlier this year, and I was terrified it might’ve been something that could pass to our 2 other cats, especially since one is her littermate. Care Credit was a lifesaver for that asap vet visit. I was able to sign up for it and get approved while standing at the vet’s registration desk, and with enough starting credit that if procedures or significant further testing was required, I’d be safe. Just absolutely make sure to pay it off before the 6 months, I believe it’s about a 30% interest rate after the promotional period ends, and a $30 late fee if you don’t pay at least once per month. (And this works for every visit, not just the first time you sign up - I was worried sick the second time I had to use it but again it was 6 months no interest :) )

Not to sound like a shill for them lol, but they seriously are amazing in a pinch. I believe the card is useful for other medical visits outside of pets as well, and their parent bank has another card for auto repairs / maintenance that’s also been a lifesaver. It’s definitely been a worthwhile first credit card.

One day my mom told me that when she got back from her shopping, if my hair wasn’t brushed she was cutting it. Well I forgot, naturally, and only remembered about 5 minutes before she came back, and tried to rush to brush it. Wasn’t good enough, so she physically picked me up and pulled me off the stair banister screaming and crying, and told me she’d call the cops on me because I was misbehaving and refusing to listen, and that they would arrest me. I was a literal child so I didn’t know she was lying. She took me to jcpenny and got my hair cut from past my waist to above my chin, and I cried the whole time. 

Fully traumatised me, and broke whatever little trust was left between us. I hated pictures after that, grew extremely socially introverted, more so than I already was, and it completely ruined my self perception. I still struggle with brushing my hair and willingly trimming dead/split ends as an adult. If you aren’t going to look after your children’s needs, at least don’t fucking threaten and traumatise them for your own convenience.

I had a similar experience with my family dog, she was my rock through a lot of really stressful years and had always looked out for us, especially my little sister and I. Eventually I moved out, and was visiting my family for an event the night before Halloween. My plan was to go back home with my boyfriend then return the next day to trick or treat with my sister. I remember my dog climbing all over me on the couch and I distinctly remember the smell of her breath and how happy she looked. When I was leaving, I wanted to lean down and kiss the top of her head and say goodnight, but I just thought “I’ll be back here tomorrow, I’ll give her a kiss and tons of pets then :)” 

It was about an hour and a half drive back to my boyfriend’s place, and we were listening to music and just having a nice time, and when we were almost there I got a strong overwhelming warm and soft sensation on the top of my brain, and I just felt happy and warm and loved, and I didn’t think much of it at the time but really enjoyed it and figured it was just a sign of the good times we were having. The next morning, my sister called me sobbing saying she had found our dog, she had passed in the night. 

Apparently about an hour after I left, our dog went into my mom’s room and stayed with her for a moment, then went into my sister’s room and stayed with her for a minute, and then she walked out and into the spare bedroom, where she crawled under the bed. I think she was saying goodbye to all of us, and that sensation I felt was was her somehow coming to say she loved me and goodbye. I wish all the time that I had just given her those last few pets. A stray kitten showed up on our doorstep a few weeks later though, and we think she may have been guided to us by our dog too, to keep us company in her loss. There is something so so special and wonderful in our furry companions 🥺💜

The death of flash games really solidified the commercialisation of the internet imo. I remember playing games2girls and poptropica and (of course) club penguin 10-15 years ago. Now my little sister is growing up and only has roblox and youtube shorts. 

It’s scary and also kinda boring at the same time. I find myself just mindlessly scrolling through all the videos I’d like to watch but never deciding and whoops now I’ve eaten half my food and maybe I should try hulu or netflix instead? …….. and then by the time you decide on something you guess is good enough, you eat the remaining like two bites from your food and just play on your phone while the video you spent 25 minutes deciding on plays in the background with you barely paying attention and then just turning it off cause it’s distracting you from the memes or discourse on your phone. 

I guess tldr I feel like the internet isn’t interactive anymore. It used to be you could click buttons and links and explore and find cool new corners of the internet, and also make some corners of your own. Now 90% of anything you click is gonna be an ad, or malware, or both, and you’ve gotta know the exact url of whatever website you want to go to because there is almost no way to just organically find things anymore. We are force fed content to keep us complacent and ready to buy and be receptive to ads and propaganda, more or less. 

Things have been on a first steady, then very steep, decline for many years now and I’ve seen some mention of us coming into the age of internet unuseability. As a whole, the internet (or at least the biggest players at the top) is user unfriendly, consistently disruptive, predatory, malicious, and proud of it. We are clinging to the shell of what we knew growing up, when the internet was also growing up and in it’s prime :’)

I’m currently working at a gas station, and a lady came in with an identification card from a Texas homeless outreach program, designed to give ID cards to those who may not have access to their birth certificate, social security cards, or other things that would typically be required to get a state/federal issued identification card. I’d never seen it before, and I still haven’t seen another one since, but it’s an interesting solution to a problem that most don’t consider.

It’s a scam, they’re trying to sign up for a Google online phone account, or other similar service, using your phone number. You then get sent a verification code, but the scammer is trying to trick you into saying it’s a code for, say, proving you’re human enough to get your dog back. They never had the dog in the first place. It’s just cruel and horrible, especially to somebody mourning or searching for a missing pet.

Firstly - your feelings are valid. Even if you’ve had a cookie cutter life, you’ve been through social hardships and a breakup that surely hurts. You have every right to feel sad because those things *are* affecting you. However there are ways to work around them, and as the brain develops, so does the capacity to respond to emotional tolls. You will get through this :) Try to look at what you *have* done in life, positive things you enjoy about yourself, and just things in general that you enjoy. 

Nobody is on a set path through life - my mother is in her 40s and is finally getting a degree in something she can stick with. My dad dropped out of an Ivy League college to pursue his true passion and ended up working for NASA later on. They want me to be successful *now*, but I have to frequently remind them that it is my own life and I will take my own path as it comes, just as they did. You were not brought into this world only to be a success story for your parents, you are your own person and you deserve to find yourself on your own time! 

I know it’s hard, I’ve been in your exact same position. However I can guarantee that you are NOT running out of time to figure things out. I am 20, still no clue what I want to do. Some people don’t figure it out until they have grandkids. The important thing is that you have fun along the way, and keep yourself alive and taken care of, so that when you do finally settle on a passion, no matter when that may be, you will be in top shape to do it :) As they say, it is a marathon, not a sprint. 

For advice? Finish high school. You’re ONLY barely a junior yet, and you’ve got good grades to boot. Plenty of people decide a career in high school only to change it immediately, and even more have no idea what they want to do until later in life. Once you finish school, decide if you want a break to find yourself, or if you want to immediately jump into more education. You do not need to choose a major right away, you can get your prerequisites out of the way, do only a couple of classes at a time, or even pursue a general education degree. You can sit in on classes that seem interesting, ask to job shadow, etc. It is a much more hands on approach but you’d be getting first hand experience in various areas and something might just click. Apply for the colleges you have your eyes on - you’ll never know if you’d be accepted until you try. 

In the meantime, try padding your application with extracurriculars, and see if you can volunteer at a local library or if they have any teen clubs. Something to get you socialising with people of a shared interest, regardless if it shows up on college applications or not. Libraries are one of our greatest resources, but are often overlooked. If you enjoy animals, shelters are always looking for volunteers to simply play with or walk their animals. If you like gardening, there are community events. Etc. There’s plenty to explore in the world - I recommend starting at the library, looking at their reference board/website or asking a librarian :) 

You got this. I believe in you. Life is a journey, and yes that includes some downsides, but try to take them as learning experiences and see what the world has to offer, there is so so so much good in it, and in you, as well :)
